fields.label: Title
fields.value: [WFAA News Clips and B-roll, ca. September 21-23, 1970]

fields.label: Description
fields.value: 0:00 - (September 23, 1970) Julian Nava and Douglas Hernandez were killed at a railroad crossing on US 80-287 near Saginaw when their truck collided with a Rock Island freight train; various shots of the aftermath of the crash (Silent).  0:32 - (September 23, 1970) North Texas State University (NTSU) students gather outside the school's administration building in protest of the dismissal of Betty Ann Duke, a graduate student and instructor, following a speech she made to freshman students at a campus rock concert during which she is accused of using “obscene language”; students are seen standing together outside on the sidewalk and in the streets; a sign reads "Freedom of Assembly"; inside, NTSU president John L. Carter Jr. speaks to a man in his office (Silent).  1:32 - Tom Landry, coach of the Dallas Cowboys, praises the performance of quarterback Roger Staubach in the team’s starting lineup and says that doesn't necessarily mean Craig Morton will remain benched (for injuries) for long; he says that experience in a starting lineup helps win national championships; he adds that Bob Hayes and Ralph Neely will both return to the starting lineup this season; Verne Lundquist reporting.  3:25 - (September 23, 1970) Gerald M. Miller, vice president of the Pleasant Grove Chamber of Commerce, says that he feels that the Dallas School Board has not kept faith with the citizens of Dallas by their postponement to appoint a replacement for school board member Jerry Wheat of Pleasant Grove (the new member is slated to come from either Pleasant Grove or South Dallas); he says that “politics” is the only reason the board hasn't found a replacement yet; Jess Brown reporting.  4:16, 6:23 - (September 23, 1970) Dr. Robert K. Osborne, one of the doctors who participated in a 9-year study on the oral diabetes drug Orinase (tolbutamide) and its potential of causing increased mortality from cardiovascular diseases, says that one of the problems of studies such as his is the long time between the start of such a study and when the data can be meaningfully compiled and gotten to practicing physicians; he describes how the drugs used to treat diabetes are all related in their basic chemical structure; additional silent footage from the press conference; Osborne has been invited to Dallas to speak at the Clinical Society of Dallas Diabetes Association and to discuss the study’s results with local doctors who have taken issue with the study which found that the drug does appear to cause earlier death; Gene Thomas reporting.  5:26, 8:46 - (September 23, 1970) Jack Strickland, regional director of the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), is interviewed, with shots of a chart titled “Consumer Price Index for Dallas, Texas”; Strickland goes on to say that Dallas and Houston currently have lower costs of living than the rest of the country, a change from the past few years when costs in the two cities were higher than the national average; Phil Reynolds reporting.  5:49 - Aftermath of a wreck involving several vehicles at a railroad crossing in the 4700 block of Scyene Road in South Dallas; Dallas police and bystanders are at the scene; businesses seen are the Gardner-Denver factory (4700 Scyene) and Atomic Liquors (4808 Scyene) (Silent).  6:18 - Brief shot of Julius Truelson, Fort Worth Independent School District (FWISD) superintendent.  6:55, 7:46 - (September 23, 1970) Dr. Charles S. Green, regional director of the Department of Health, Education and Welfare (HEW), holds a press conference with fellow HEW official Dan Reed to announce the appointment of Dr. Quinten S. Mathews (seated at far left) as deputy regional director of HEW (Silent); in an interview, Green says that there's a fragmented federal delivery mechanism, with several agencies dealing with child-related issues, and that in the years to come, the country will see a greater interest in preschool education; he goes on to say that he doesn't see socialized medicine happening in this country but, rather, that there will be a pluralism involving private and government sectors.  7:25 - (September 23, 1970) Brief shot of Dallas sports magnate Lamar Hunt who has just been named Chairman of the South Central Region of the National Alliance of Businessmen (NAB).  9:25 - (September 23, 1970) Texas Instruments Inc. (TI) – the largest employer in Dallas County – has just laid off 1,210 employees; TI would not allow reporters to interview employees on their property, so reporter Jim Mitchell stands outside the fence surrounding the company’s parking lot as employees leave in their cars during the shift change; the company’s reason for the mass layoff was the “continued softness in the market for discrete semiconductors such as transistors and diodes.”  10:19 - (September 23, 1970) A meeting of the Dallas School Board is underway with Dr. Nolan Estes, Dallas Independent School District superintendent, presiding (Silent).  11:04, 22:11- (September 22, 1970) R. L. Thornton Jr., chairman of the Mercantile National Bank, has been named Chairman of the United Negro College Fund drive in Texas; Thornton says that the general public’s perception of historically Black colleges and universities (HBCU) has improved over the years; additional silent footage from the interview; Teel Salaun reporting.  11:30, 21:40 - (September 22, 1970) Terry Means, newly-elected student body president of Southern Methodist University (SMU), discusses the shared governance plan the university has adopted, which involves the faculty, the administration, and the student body, saying that he hopes that all three entities can work together as a community and that focusing on confrontation politics is antithetical to the university's mission; additional footage from the interview (President George H. W. Bush appointed Means to the federal bench as a District Judge in 1991); Phil Reynolds reporting.  12:23 - (September 22, 1970) Dr. James W. Turpin, founder of Project Concern, describes his experience as a medical missionary in Vietnam and the shooting of one his medical assistants by a member of the Viet Cong; he says there will be no improvement in Vietnam without infrastructure and employment opportunities; Turpin, a San Diego doctor, is in Fort Worth to accept a donated mobile home which will be used as a mobile medical-dental clinic to serve Native American residents in the Bisti area of New Mexico; Art Sinclair reporting.  13:12, 20:51 - (September 22, 1970) Lakshmi Kant Jha, India’s ambassador to the United States, says that the United Nations (UN) resolution for Israeli withdrawal should be honored, that Israel's identity as a nation should be protected, and that any adjustments made should be negotiated; additional silent shots from the interview; Jha is in Dallas to address the Dallas Council on World Affairs; Gene Thomas reporting.  14:26 - (September 22, 1970) Ralph Ingram Rogers, in handcuffs, is escorted from the federal courthouse in Fort Worth to a waiting car; he had just been arraigned on charges of dealing in counterfeit money following an earlier seizure of $70,000 in fake bills by Secret Service agents (Silent).  15:00 - (September 22, 1970) 16-year-old Curtis “Corky” Simmons is on trial for the murder of service station attendant Loyd Choate in Fort Worth; among those seen in the courtroom are Simmons, Sheriff’s Dept. investigator B. D. Griffin (on the witness stand), Simmons’ defense attorneys Roland Hill Jr. (blue suit) and Charles Mays, and District Judge Gordon Gray (Silent).  15:43 - Fred Taylor, head football coach for Texas Christian University (TCU), talks about their upcoming matchup against the Wisconsin Badgers and the recent performance of quarterback Steve Judy against Purdue; he says the secondary is holding up well and that he’s pleased with them; Jerry Haynes reporting.  17:02, 21:15 - The plans of the Fort Worth park and recreation department to spend $60,000 on improving the wooded River Bend Park in West Fort Worth are on hold because nearby homeowners are protesting, saying they fear the park will attract “hippies and dope and electric music”; in an interview, R. F. “Bob” Snakard, the attorney for the homeowners, says they are ready to work with the park department to make the area open to children, Boy Scouts, and others; in another interview, Fort Worth City Councilman Ted C. Peters says he sees both points of view and that “undesirable” people at area parks is a problem in and of itself; additional silent footage of the interview with Peters; Jerry Taff reporting.  19:40 - (September 22, 1970) Dallas Fire Chief C. N. Penn presents awards at Fire Station No. 34 (8003 Lake June Road in Pleasant Grove) to Harvie Lee, Larry Roberts, Charles E. Hall, Jessie T. Reed, and George E. Beck, who had rescued an accident victim trapped in an automobile; various shots from the ceremony (Silent). 22:29 - Brief shot of J. Erik Jonsson, mayor of Dallas (Silent).  22:43 - (September 22, 1970) Herman H. Dinsmore, former editor of the international edition of the New York Times, believes that his former employer regularly distorts the news in order to shape public opinion and exerts too much influence on the media, on the President, on Congress, and on college administrators; he says that the Times’ influence is interlocking with the government, citing the newspaper’s call to withdraw from the Vietnam War, which he believes has influenced the American government’s foreign policy decisions; Dinsmore is in Dallas to speak to a John Birch Society-affiliated group; Gene Thomas reporting.  23:51, 27:20 - A man says that this has been a problem since the beginning of the Dallas-Fort Worth Regional Airport project and has continued through 4 or 5 phases of work so far; he goes on to say that the airport board is refusing to take autonomous power and is passing the buck along to the City Councils of Dallas and Fort Worth; because nobody appears to be in charge, it is impossible to negotiate union wages for those involved in the airport’s construction; Jay Lewis reporting.  24:07, 28:46 - A report on the gathering of local senior citizens at a forum held at the Texas Bank in Dallas where they will asked their opinions about what they would like to see addressed at the Second White House Conference on Aging in 1971; various shots of attendees at the meeting filling out forms (Silent); a woman is interviewed and says that the first need is an increase in retirement benefits; another woman says that people on a fixed income are hurt by increased taxes, and tax issues are of primary importance to senior citizens; Gene Thomas reporting.  25:19 - (September 21, 1970) The United Fund (UF) drive kicks off in downtown Dallas with the temporary renaming of Main Street as “United Way”; in front of City Hall, UF campaign chairman Avery Mays lifts UF poster girl Marsha Gail Waldie from her wheelchair and onto his shoulder; the Dallas City Council members stand outside during the ceremony; Mayor J. Erik Jonsson hands the new street sign reading “United Way” to Miss United Fund Nancy Bonetti who sits on a ladder at the corner of Main and Harwood (Silent).  25:55 - (September 21, 1970) The Tarrant County tax department needs more space and a centralized office and had looked into purchasing a building at 116 Commerce in Fort Worth, but the Commissioners Court is now discussing the possibility of building an east wing onto the old county courthouse and are looking into funding options for the construction; Art Sinclair reporting.  26:48, 28:09 - A man is interviewed; he goes on to say that the fire department has lost 16 firefighters since 1969; Carl Mayo reporting.  28:39 - Brief shot of Bonnie Singleton, wife of Capt. Jerry Singleton who was shot down in 1965 and is a North Vietnamese prisoner of war (POW); Mrs. Singleton has recently received positive letters from her husband, whom she had feared might be in grave health (Silent).
